title: Molecular detection of HPV in fragmented DNA from cervical cancer biopsies using double-nested PCR
author: Tawe, Grover, et al.

steps.title: Dewax and rehydrate FFPE tissue
steps.instruction: Place tissue sections in 15 ml tubes, add xylene and incubate for 18 h; then replace with 100 % ethanol for another 18 h; finally transfer sequentially to 95 %, 80 %, 70 % and 50 % ethanol, incubating 1 h in each concentration, and repeat the one‑hour incubations for each concentration three times to achieve gradual re‑hydration.

steps.title: Assess DNA extraction quality
steps.instruction: Perform PCR amplification of a 107 bp fragment of the human CYP2C8 gene using the degenerate primers CYP2C8‑F (AAGACACCAAGCATCACTGGA) and CYP2C8‑R (GAAATCAAAATACTGATCTGTTGC) as an extraction control; include human genomic DNA as a positive control and run products on a 2 % agarose gel.

steps.title: Outer PCR with SB01/02 primers
steps.instruction: Set up a 20 µl PCR containing 3 µl of extracted DNA template, SB01/02 primer pair (see Table 1), 3.5 mM MgCl₂, and the remaining master mix components; run the thermal profile from Table 2: pre‑denaturation 95 °C 5 min, denaturation 95 °C 1 min, annealing 42 °C 1 min, extension 72 °C 1 min, then 20 cycles of 95 °C 20 s, 42 °C 40 s, 72 °C 1 min, finishing with a final extension at 72 °C for 10 min. Include positive and negative controls in the same run.

steps.title: Nested PCR with MY09/11 primers
steps.instruction: Using 3 µl of the outer‑PCR product as template, prepare a 20 µl reaction with MY09/11 primers (Table 1) and 3.5 mM MgCl₂; thermal cycling: pre‑denaturation 95 °C 5 min, denaturation 95 °C 15 s, annealing 50 °C 1 min, extension 72 °C 1 min, followed by a final extension at 72 °C for 10 min (repeat cycles as indicated in Table 2). Run positive, negative and extraction‑control samples in parallel. Resolve PCR products on a 2.5 % agarose gel stained with ethidium bromide; a ~450 bp band indicates a positive result.

steps.title: RFLP typing of nested‑PCR positives
steps.instruction: Digest the ~450 bp nested‑PCR amplicons with HpyCH4V restriction enzyme under the conditions described by Cheng et al. [30]; separate fragments on a 4 % MetaPhor™ agarose gel (Lonza) stained with ethidium bromide to determine HPV genotype.

steps.title: Double‑nested PCR with GP5/6 primers
steps.instruction: Take 3 µl of the nested‑PCR product and add to a 20 µl reaction containing GP5/6 primers (Table 1) and 2.5 mM MgCl₂; thermal profile (Table 2): pre‑denaturation 95 °C 10 min, denaturation 95 °C 30 s, annealing 50 °C 40 s, extension 72 °C 30 s, final extension 72 °C 10 min. Include appropriate positive, negative and contamination‑control samples. Visualise the ~150 bp amplicons on a 2 % agarose gel stained with ethidium bromide.

steps.title: Include contamination controls
steps.instruction: At each PCR stage (outer, nested, double‑nested) run no‑template controls and reagent‑only controls to monitor for possible contamination; if any control shows amplification, halt the diagnostic workflow until the source of contamination is identified and eliminated.
